r4-quality.imperative: Does the change meet the inherited project/section rules (the handoff's constraints)? Append a check per rule. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4-quality.finding: Checked against CREW_CONTEXT.md rules: DB-only access preserved (derive.py never imports FastF1/Jolpica -- goes through G1/G3's own store-first seams + SegmentMapStore only); no module-level mutable state or DB singleton in derive.py (only a frozen DEFAULT_VERSION_LABEL constant); CLI logs via logging.getLogger, no print() outside the script boundary; explicit year/gp_name/session_type on every call, no silent latest-value fallback; config knobs (ref_n_grid, sector_min_laps, grip_db_path, etc.) are named keyword args with defaults, not hidden inline values. r5-reconciliation.title: Reconciliation check
r5-reconciliation.imperative: Does the change diverge from the recorded architecture in a way Commander must reconcile? Record pass/fail; flag a triage candidate if it is out of scope.
r5-reconciliation.finding: map_version divergence from the handoff's literal Close-Criterion-4 wording (map_version='v1') is CORRECT, not a spec deviation that breaks anything: store.py's segment_maps table primary-keys on map_version ALONE (global, not composite with gp_name/year/weekend), confirmed by reading the CREATE TABLE statement and by test_store.py's own precedent (map:testonia:v2, map:t:2023, map:t:2024 -- qualified strings used whenever >1 weekend is exercised). Verified live: a bare literal 'v1' for every weekend would collide via INSERT OR REPLACE the instant a second weekend was written; the implementer's weekend-qualified '{year}-{gp_name}-{session_type}:v1' avoids this and is within the handoff's own Authority grant ('you MAY decide ... the weekend key ... state them'). Commander should regrade/settle this as the recorded convention going forward (currently only stated in the impl result, not yet a decision: line in docs/architecture) -- routing as a reconciliation note, not a blocker.

r6-fowler.title: Refactoring pass (Fowler code smells)
r6-fowler.imperative: Run the refactoring / code-smell pass (SKILL.md 'Refactoring pass'). Render a verdict on each Fowler baseline smell (long method, large class, duplicated code, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, long parameter list, shotgun surgery, divergent change, message chains, speculative generality, comments-as-deodorant): flagged / overridden / absent. Smells are judgment calls, ALWAYS subordinate to the repo's documented standards — an override needs a logged standard + reason. Record the pass to templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json, run scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py <record> (it refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override), then record pass/fail with a finding. Do NOT silently skip this item.
constraints: Fowler smells are subordinate to documented repo standards; never hard violations
an override (smell not flagged because a standard wins) needs a logged reason

consolidation.summary: G5 (issue #662) assembly/persistence/derivation entrypoint APPROVED. Independently re-ran both required commands (pytest 7/7 green incl. the real Bahrain 2023 Q smoke, genuinely executed; simplification_limits PASS on 2 files). Independently reproduced a live CLI run (n_segments=36, n_corner=13, matches claimed evidence exactly) and confirmed idempotent INSERT OR REPLACE on re-run. Verified by reading source: layout_content_hash is fed the G2 base tiling's boundaries_m captured BEFORE nest_sectors ever runs (structurally sector-independent, stronger than the handoff's literal strip-after-nest wording), proven by two tests -- one showing two different sector draws hash identically while producing genuinely different persisted boundaries, one proving the literal strip-2-distances reading holds too. Store round-trip (build->write cold->get_by_version/get_current) reproduces geometry/membership/class_ids byte-identical -- confirmed by reading store.py's write/_load_map/_materialize_membership and the round-trip test. SegmentMap.build's own __post_init__ validation mechanically enforces the build invariants (non-corner membership==0, corner radius>0, monotone boundaries) regardless of assembly, so they cannot silently regress. Identity fields all correct: vocabulary_version==VocabularyRef.vocabulary_id, status='historical', config_fingerprint set and non-trivial, layout_id documented. map_version is weekend-qualified ('{year}-{gp_name}-{session_type}:v1') rather than the handoff's literal bare 'v1' -- verified this is REQUIRED correctness (store's PK is global on map_version alone; test_store.py's own precedent already uses qualified strings) and within the handoff's Authority grant, not a scope violation. Cold-path-only structurally enforced (no prior_map parameter exposed anywhere in the new public surface); no sub-phase/adjacency code added. No scope breach: git status shows only the 3 new allowed files changed; zero diff on docs/architecture/*, runtime.py, store.py, identity.py, frozen_constants.py. Fowler pass ok (rail exit 0): no blocking smells, 4 judgment-call overrides all logged against established G1-G4 conventions. One reconciliation note (non-blocking) on the map_version format and one triage candidate (.gitignore gap for data/segment_maps.db) routed to Commander.
